star.description: One party has a top-decile historical Senate candidate relative to its opponent. The lower decile and known-history indicators enter separately. Both-party star presence cancels in this relative comparison.
star.reading: The historical star estimates are imprecise and include zero. There are 36 top-decile nominee appearances in the full House sample and 23 in the governor sample. Recent held-out samples contain only 2 House star cases and 0 governor star cases, so they cannot establish a reliable modern all-star effect.
star.coverage: House: 3,389 districts across 499 state elections and 49 states, each state election weighted equally. Governor: 285 races in 43 states. *Only one matched House district contributes in 2022 because most boundaries changed. Coefficient intervals allow correlation within states.

continuous.description: Each 10-point increase in the Democratic-versus-Republican Senate historical-performance advantage. The outcome is the Democratic vote share in the other office. This continuous comparison is the primary statistical test.
continuous.reading: Across the full history, both estimates include zero. A separate House model refitted only on 2016–2022 is positive (+2.86 points), so the relationship is sensitive to the period. The fixed historical model does not improve held-out teammate forecasts. This does not establish a stable causal spillover.
continuous.coverage: House: 3,389 districts across 499 state elections and 49 states, each state election weighted equally. Governor: 285 races in 43 states. *Only one matched House district contributes in 2022 because most boundaries changed. Coefficient intervals allow correlation within states.

forecast_note: MAE is percentage points; positive improvement means less error. House fits through 2014 before its test; governor keeps its fit through 2008. These are within-office comparisons, not a ranking across offices. The predictor is continuous strength. Only 2 top-decile House cases and no top-decile governor cases occur in these test samples, so this is not an out-of-time validation of exceptional candidates specifically.
